code:
# The "magic number" - all ELF files start with these 4 bytes:
xxd hello | head -1
# 7f 45 4c 46  -> \x7f E L F

# Full ELF header:
readelf -h hello
# Magic:   7f 45 4c 46 02 01 01 00  ...
# Class:   ELF64 (64-bit)
# Data:    2's complement, little endian
# Type:    EXEC (executable file)
# Machine: Advanced Micro Devices X86-64
# Entry:   0x401060  <- this is where execution starts (_start, not main!)
# PH off:  64       <- program header table offset
# SH off:  ...      <- section header table offset

# Sections:
readelf -S hello
# [Nr] Name       Type    Address    Size
# [13] .text      PROGBITS 0x401060  0x...  AX (alloc+execute)
# [15] .rodata    PROGBITS 0x...     0x...  A  (alloc, read-only)
# [24] .data      PROGBITS 0x...     0x...  WA (write+alloc)
# [25] .bss       NOBITS   0x...     0x...  WA (zero-filled)

# Disassemble:
objdump -d hello | head -40
description: These commands inspect ELF bytes, header fields, sections, and disassembled instructions.

steps.description: xxd shows the four-byte ELF magic number at the start of the file.
readelf -h displays header fields, including file class, machine, entry address, and header-table offsets.
readelf -S lists sections such as code, read-only data, initialized data, and zero-filled data.
objdump disassembles the first forty lines of the executable.

title: Inspect an ELF executable
